newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Parliament demands ban on human cloning.
newsitem.headline: EU Parliament demands ban on human cloning.

text.p: The European Parliament, reacting to the successful cloning of an adult sheep, called on Wednesday for a worldwide ban on the cloning of humans and strict controls on the cloning of animals.

"The cloning of human beings, whether experimentally, in the context of fertility treatment, preimplantaton diagnosis, tissue transplantation or for any other purpose whatsoever, cannot under any circumstances be justified or tolerated by any society," the EU assembly said in a resolution.
The European Union should immediately stop all funding to research into human cloning and EU governments should impose penal sanctions on anyone found defying the ban, Euro-MPs said.

After a lengthy debate on animal cloning for science, medicine and farming, the assemnbly decided against a ban but urged the EU to adopt laws which would strictly control the technique, protect human health and ensure no species was allowed to die out or have its gene pool limited.

It urged the EU to take a lead in getting a binding international agreement to respect these principles worldwide and called for the creation of an open and democratic EU ethics committee to examine the implications of gene technology and monitor developments in this field.
EU Research Commissioner Edith Cresson told the parliament on Tuesday the EU opposed research into human cloning.

The former French socialist prime minister announced that the European Commission had asked its biotechnology ethics committee, an independent advisory body, to report back on the implications of the sheep cloning experiment by May.
